Continuous feedings are administered over 8 to 24 hours
daily, using a pump to control the feeding rate. Continuous 
feedings are typically preferred in the acute care setting as GI
tolerance is maximized with this delivery. Additionally, they 
are easier and less time consuming for staﬀ  to administer than
bolus or intermittent feedings. Using a pump to deliver feed-
ings slowly at a continuous rate may improve feeding tolerance,
but intermittent feedings are also well tolerated by individual 
patients. A disadvantage of continuous feeding is the expense
